Suppose the rotation period of this planet is T, the radius is R, and the gravitational constant is G. Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal forces of the objects placed at the two points A and B as they rotate with the planet is $\frac{m_A}{\sqrt{3}m_B}$

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Simplify Kepler-452b into the model shown in the figure: MN is the rotation axis of this planet; A and B are two points on the surface of this planet; the angles between the lines OA and OB connecting them with the center of the planet O and MN are respectively α=30° and β=60°; objects with masses respectively $m_A$ and $m_B$ are placed at the two points A and B. Suppose the rotation period of this planet is T and the radius is R. Find the ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal forces of the objects placed at the two points A and B as they rotate with the planet.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: The ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal forces of the objects placed at the two points A and B as they rotate with the planet is $\frac{m_A}{\sqrt{3}m_B}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Simplify Kepler-452b into the model shown in the figure: MN is the rotation axis of this planet; A and B are two points on the surface of this planet; the angles between the lines OA and OB connecting them with the center of the planet O and MN are respectively α=30° and β=60°; objects with masses respectively $m_A$ and $m_B$ are placed at the two points A and B. Suppose the rotation period of this planet is T and the radius is R. Find the ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal forces of the objects placed at the two points A and B as they rotate with the planet.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal forces of the objects placed at the two points A and B as they rotate with the planet is $\frac{m_A}{\sqrt{3}m_B}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the planet is drawn as a circle; the vertical straight line MN passes through the center of the sphere O, representing the rotation axis; the two points A and B are on the circumference, and OA and OB are both radii from the center of the sphere O to the surface; the figure marks the angle between OA and the rotation axis MN as α, and the angle between OB and the rotation axis MN as β. The problem gives α=30° and β=60°, the planet radius is R, and the rotation period is T. Reasoning: When an object rotates with the planet and undergoes circular motion, the radius of the circular motion is not the sphere radius R, but the perpendicular distance from that point to the rotation axis MN. Therefore r_A=R sinα, r_B=R sinβ. Points A and B rotate with the same planet, so their angular velocities are the same, ω=2π/T. The centripetal force F=mω^2r, so F_A/F_B=(m_Aω^2R sin30°)/(m_Bω^2R sin60°). Canceling ω^2R gives F_A/F_B=(m_A/m_B)·(1/2)/(√3/2)=m_A/(√3m_B).
